title: Copying and clearing a tape word
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $\Gamma$ be an alphabet, and let $x$ be an input word. Choose distinct work tapes $\mathrm{src},\mathrm{dst}$ and a word $w\in\Gamma^*$. Suppose a configuration $d$ starts in the copy phase and, for every integer offset $p$ with $-1\le p\le |w|$, tape $\mathrm{src}$ at its head position plus $p$ contains the symbol of $w$ at offset $p$ (and is blank outside the word). After $4|w|+5$ steps, the machine is in its final phase, tape $\mathrm{src}$ is blank on the $|w|$ cells beginning at its original head position, and tape $\mathrm{dst}$ contains a copy of $w$ on the $|w|$ cells beginning at its original head position; all other cells and configuration data are unchanged. The final phase is not reached earlier, and at every time up to and including this one, every work-tape head is within distance $|w|+1$ of its initial position.
hypotheses_covered: distinct source and destination tape indices
initial state is the copy machine's sweep phase
source tape agrees with the buffered word at offsets $-1$ through $|w|$
